## Job Market Paper

::: {.paper}
::: {.paper-title}
Wages, amenities and the value of formal employment: A structural approach for Mexico [Paper](files/Documents/JMP/Siachoque_JMP.pdf){.paper-link target="_blank"}
:::

<details class="abstract">
<summary>Abstract</summary>
<div class="abstract-body">
Informal employment is high and persistent in low- and middle-income economies;
however, evidence suggests that workers move between informal and formal jobs
frequently. Using data for Mexico, I document that informal-to-formal transitions
are more frequent than transitions in the opposite direction, that most occur
within the same firm, and that these generate only modest immediate wage gains.
I use a two-sector search model with on-the-job search to estimate workers'
willingness to pay for a formal job, which captures both the wage and the
non-wage reasons to accept one. I decompose the willingness to pay into
sector-specific amenities, employment stability, and future job opportunities,
including formal offers from the current employer. At the median informal wage,
high-skilled workers are willing to pay USD 40–45 per month for a formal job,
below its social-security cost, while low-skilled workers are close to
indifferent. I find that once the within-firm route is included, the value of
remaining informal rises as workers wait for better future formal employment
opportunities in the same firm.
</div>
</details>
:::
